title: An archive in its speakers’ language
proposal: Language resources and speech transcription could support an archive that speakers can review and control.
untested: This record does not establish transcription quality in the chosen language, or that a community wants an archive.
experiment: With permission, try one short recording. Ask its speaker to correct the transcript and choose what may be kept.
goal: Help speakers preserve stories in their own language, with control over how they are shared.

title: More ways into a shared story
proposal: Speech transcripts and image descriptions could offer different ways to access a story with audio and pictures.
untested: Neither record establishes that this combination meets the accessibility needs of its intended readers.
experiment: Invite one willing reader to assess a short transcript and a description of one non-sensitive image. Ask which details are missing.
goal: Make a story with audio and pictures easier to access in different ways.

title: A warning people can understand
proposal: Flood forecasts and speaker-led language work could help a local team communicate a warning in a language people use.
untested: Local forecast coverage, translation accuracy and a trusted response channel require separate checks. The combination has not been evaluated here.
experiment: Review an old, non-live warning with a local speaker and responder. Compare the forecast’s meaning with the proposed message before considering a live use.
goal: Explore how a local team could make flood information understandable and useful to its community.

title: From a molecular question to a lab test
proposal: Protein-structure resources and the enzyme research example suggest a route for developing an experimentally testable biological question.
untested: This is a conceptual bridge. The sources here do not establish that AlphaFold produced FAST-PETase or that a proposed enzyme will work.
experiment: With a qualified researcher, choose one molecular question and separate a structural prediction from the laboratory result needed to evaluate it.
goal: Develop a biological research question with a clear boundary between a model prediction and an experimental result.
